tool.name: MetaDAVis
tool.description: Interactive analysis and visualization of 16S and whole-metagenome sequencing results

param.name: otu_table
param.label: OTU / feature table (optional)
param.help: Feature count table in phyloseq layout: features (OTUs, ASVs or other features) in the rows, the first column holding the feature id, and one column per sample. Tab or comma separated, the separator is detected from the header.

param.name: taxonomy_table
param.label: Taxonomy table (optional)
param.help: Taxonomy assignment for the features of the OTU table: features in the rows, the first column holding the same feature ids, and one column per taxonomic rank (Kingdom to Species). Rank prefixes such as d__ or p__ are stripped. Features missing from this table are reported as Unclassified.

param.name: metadata_table
param.label: Sample metadata (optional)
param.help: Sample annotations: the first column holds the sample ids, which have to match the sample columns of the OTU table. The column picked below is used as the condition/group for the comparisons.

param.name: condition_column
param.label: Grouping condition column (optional)
param.help: Column of the sample metadata holding the grouping condition. Samples are grouped by this column in all comparisons. The application only ever works with two metadata columns, the sample ids and this one, so the table is reduced to those before the analysis: any further annotation columns are dropped. Pick the second column if your metadata is the usual sample id plus condition layout; leaving this empty does the same.

tool.help:
`MetaDAVis <https://github.com/GudaLab/MetaDAVis>`_ is a browser based R Shiny application for analyzing and visualizing 16S and whole-metagenome sequencing results from kingdom to species level.
.. class:: infomark
**Results are sent to your Galaxy history.** Every table and plot has a *Send to Galaxy* button next to its download button, which puts the file into the history of this session, where the next tool can use it. The *Run* tab offers a bulk download of all analyses you have completed during the session as a single ZIP archive, which can be sent the same way.
**Input datasets.** The three tables you select here are staged and pre-loaded into the application as the *Galaxy input* format in the *Upload files* tab. Open the tool, choose *Galaxy input* and press *Submit* to analyse them. Use *Grouping condition column* to say which column of the metadata table holds the condition the samples are grouped by; the taxonomic level to display and all other options are set inside the application. You can also ignore the pre-loaded data and upload your own files from within the browser, or use the built-in example data.
What this tool provides:
#. Data summary, taxonomy and metadata tables #. Group and individual abundance distribution #. Alpha and beta diversity analysis #. Dimension reduction (PCA 2D/3D, t-SNE, UMAP) #. Correlation analysis (taxa, samples, taxa-condition) #. Heatmaps #. Differential abundance for two-group and multi-group comparisons (Wilcoxon, t-test, metagenomeSeq, DESeq2, LEfSe, MaAsLin3, limma-voom, edgeR, Kruskal-Wallis, ANOVA)
.. class:: infomark
**Citation**
Jagadesan S, Guda C (2025) MetaDAVis: An R shiny application for metagenomic data analysis and visualization. PLoS ONE 20(4): e0319949.
